name: Starter: Slovenian
about: Slovenian word order and cases in real, everyday sentences.

words.delati: to do, to make; to work
words.imeti se: to be doing, to fare (kako se imaš: how are you)
words.všeč: pleasing (mi je všeč: I like it)
words.rad: likes to, gladly (masculine; feminine rada; rad bi, rada bi: would like)
words.kino: movie theater (v kino: to the movies)
words.zebsti: to feel cold (zebe me: I'm cold)

oprostite.about: To get someone's attention or say sorry: polite to one person, or to more than one; one friend gets Oprosti.

concept.line: The verb's ending marks the person: (jaz) živim, (ti) živiš, (on, ona) živi, (mi) živimo, (oni) živijo.
A Slovenian verb marks person and number, so jaz (I), ti (you) and mi (we) are usually left out when it's clear who: Živim v majhnem stanovanju (I live in a small apartment).

words.means: si = you are; nisem = I am not

concept.line: Short unstressed words like sem, si, je, se, mi, ti, me and te follow the first word or phrase: Včeraj sem bil doma; Kako ti je ime?; Jutri te pokličem.

words.means: imam = I have; imaš = you have; nimam = I do not have

concept.line: Slovenian nouns are masculine, feminine or neuter (a consonant is often masculine, -a often feminine, -o or -e often neuter), and the words with them match: moj brat, moja mama.

words.means: govoriš = you speak; govorim = I speak
razumem = I understand; razumeš = you understand

concept.line: The accusative marks many direct objects (kava becomes Pijem kavo), the one who feels the cold in Zebe me (I'm cold), and follows v and na for where you're going and v for days: v trgovino, na plažo, v soboto.

words.means: živim = I live; živiš = you live; živi = lives

concept.line: Slovenian has no words for a, an or the; context and word order do their work: Sem učitelj; Na mizi je knjiga.

words.means: delam = I work; delati = to work
